rep.angle: lead with a recent hiring push you noticed
rep.name: Sara

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sam Whitfield. I have fifteen minutes, go ahead.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Sam, Sara at HyperSale. I noticed Northwind’s sales hiring push; may I ask how you’re ensuring new reps are buyer-ready before live calls?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Our VP of Sales owns that process. Why is this worth forty-eight thousand dollars?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair question: $48,000 equips 40 reps with realistic practice and quote-backed scoring, exposing coaching gaps before quota time. What does delayed ramp cost annually?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: A new rep costs us about $7,500 a month fully loaded. How many ramp months do you remove, across how many hires, and can you get below $35,000?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I can’t credibly promise months before a baseline; a 30-day pilot will measure it. Below $35,000 requires narrower scope—how many hires this year?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: The hiring plan isn’t final. Price the 30-day pilot separately and give me a 40-rep annual option at or below $35,000; what ramp-time reduction would the pilot need to demonstrate?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: $5,000 pilot, credited; $35,000 annually for 40 requires two years. If it shows 4.7 rep-months annualized, review Thursday at two with you and VP Sales?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Four-point-seven rep-months only gets me to break-even; I’d need at least seven, or $52,500 in annualized savings. I won’t commit for two years—make it $35,000 for one year, lower the credited pilot to $3,000, and give me the calendar date for the review with our VP of Sales.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: $3,000 credited pilot; $35,000 prepaid annual term for 40 if it validates seven rep-months. Can you and your VP review Thursday, November 5, at two?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thursday, November 5 at two works; include the baseline, measurement method for seven rep-months, and the $3,000 credit. Send me the business case and we'll take it from there.
